findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data object does not update updatedAt (and can throw)
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache ends with `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credentialId, {})`. The comment says it updates SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, but an empty `data` object contains no fields, so Prisma will either fail validation ("at least one field") or perform a no-op; in either case `updatedAt` is not bumped because @updatedAt is only refreshed when an update actually writes fields. The intended cache-refresh timestamp tracking therefore silently never happens. Pass an explicit field (or rely on a dedicated touch), e.g. `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` if that is the goal.

findings.title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status
findings.body: After a successful cache deletion the component only calls the optional `onSuccess` callback (which in SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper is `props.onChanged` and may be undefined). Unlike the disconnect mutation, there is no `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`, so the "Cache Status / Last updated" entry in the dropdown keeps showing the old timestamp until a full page reload or unrelated refetch. Add the same invalidation used in disconnectMutation's onSettled.

findings.title: deleteCacheHandler throws plain Error instead of a TRPCError, producing an opaque internal server error
findings.body: When the credential is not found or not owned by the user, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. In cal.com's tRPC setup plain errors are masked as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, so the client shows the generic "Error deleting cache" message with no way to distinguish a permission problem. Throw a TRPCError with code UNAUTHORIZED/NOT_FOUND instead. Also note that for delegated (in-memory) credentials the UI passes a negative credentialId which will always land on this error path.

findings.title: sed -i '' -E is macOS-only and fails on Linux
findings.body: The script uses `sed -i '' -E "..." "$ENV_FILE"`. The `sed -i ''` (empty backup suffix) syntax only works on BSD/macOS sed; on GNU/Linux sed it fails with "can't read : No such file or directory". This dev script is not portable to the Linux environments most contributors use. Use `sed -i.bak -E ... && rm -f "$ENV_FILE.bak"` or detect the platform.

findings.title: Extra groupBy DB query runs on every connectedCalendars call even when no cache can exist
findings.body: The handler unconditionally instantiates CalendarCacheRepository and runs a groupBy over calendarCache for all credentialIds on every invocation of this very hot query (used by onboarding, settings, booking pages). Consider guarding the extra round-trip (e.g. only query when there is at least one Google Calendar credential, or fold the max(updatedAt) into the existing credential fetch) to avoid adding latency to every connectedCalendars request.

findings.title: Behavior change: Alert rows now hide disconnect button when disableConnectionModification is set
findings.body: Previously, the error/Alert branch rendered the disconnect control whenever `!connectedCalendar.delegationCredentialId` regardless of `disableConnectionModification`; the new CredentialActionsDropdown applies `disableConnectionModification` in both branches, so users in contexts that pass that flag (e.g. certain embed/event-type scopes) lose the ability to remove a broken integration from the Alert row where it was previously available. If intentional, confirm; otherwise pass the prop only for the non-Alert branch.
